Keiko Ochi, Ph.D.

Speech Processing, Conversational AI, Affective Computing, Human-Robot Interaction
Project Assistant Professor, Kyoto University, Japan

Research Overview

My research focuses on the dynamics of human spoken communication, from speech prosody and interpersonal coordination to conversational AI and human–robot interaction.

I am particularly interested in how information beyond words—such as intonation, rhythm, emotion, and turn-taking—shapes human communication, and how these features can be modeled computationally.

My early research focused on prosody modeling and expressive speech synthesis. I subsequently expanded my work to clinical speech research, investigating stuttering and communication characteristics in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), including prosodic entrainment between conversational partners.

More recently, I have developed attentive-listening dialogue systems and communication robots, incorporating adaptive backchannels and natural conversational behaviors. These systems have been evaluated in real-world settings, including psychiatric rehabilitation and older-adult care.

My current research explores long-context modeling of spoken interaction using state-space models such as S4 and Mamba. I am also investigating speech-based approaches to cognitive and voice health, with the aim of connecting computational models of communication to clinical applications and neuroimaging research.


🩺Speech Processing & Clinical Speech Research

Prosody modeling, expressive speech synthesis, stuttering, voice health, and acoustic markers of communication differences.

🗣️Conversational AI & Human–Robot Interaction

Turn-taking, adaptive backchannels, conversational entrainment, and attentive-listening robots for human-centered applications.

🔧Long-Sequence Modeling & Multimodal Communication

State-space models, temporal dynamics of dialogue, emotion, and the integration of speech with behavioral and neuroimaging data.
